text:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up: we saw the service-processor memory leak again (3rd time in ~8 weeks). We need a small triage appendix in the playbook with: immediate checks, exact commands we used, and a clear escalation path. Also assign owners + due dates for the runbook + a recurring review cadence. Thoughts?

devon: I'll take ownership of the runbook appendix. Plan: add 'Immediate Triage' checklist, safe restart steps, and the PromQL we used for the spike. I'll open a PR by Tue EOD.

oliver: I'll own the monitoring side: add a Prometheus alert for resident_memory_bytes > 1.2Gi for 5m and a weekly canary job to catch slow leaks. ETA 72h.

maria: thanks. please include the exact PromQL we ran and the graph link. put the query under "Detect" so on-call can copy-paste.

oliver: PromQL:```promql
sum by (instance) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job="service-processor"})
```

rachel: for safe restarts, we used a rolling restart to avoid dropping inflight messages. snippet I used:```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/service-processor -n prod
# wait for readiness
kubectl get pods -l app=service-processor -n prod -o wide
```

rachel: if rolling restart doesn't recover and OOMs keep happening, escalate to eng-sre after second attempt. Escalation chain: on-call -> eng-sre -> platform-lead (pager). Also include a template message for paging.

ops-bot: Suggested escalation message: "INCIDENT: service-processor memory growth; repeated restarts x2; immediate investigation required."

maria: include the kubectl logs grep we ran to spot OOM kills:```bash
kubectl logs <pod> -n prod --since=2h | grep -i "Killed process" || true
```

oliver: on the monitoring side, I'll add a 3-stage alert: warning (1m, 900Mi), critical (5m, 1.2Gi) and pager only on critical. Also add a 10m auto-silence on flapping.

devon: runbook outline I'm planning to add: 1) Detect (PromQL + dashboard link), 2) Quick checks (pod memory, restart count, consumer lag), 3) Commands (safe restart, logs grep), 4) When to escalate, 5) Post-restart validation checklist, 6) Links to JIRA action RW-3680.

maria: RW-3680 will have owners and timeline. devon, can you also add a short 'why this matters' blurb so reviewers understand recurrence risk?

devon: yup - short paragraph explaining recurrence & impact, plus a rollback plan if restart causes consumer lag to spike.

rachel: validation steps after restart: check consumer lag < 200 for key topics and verify memory trend decreases over 30m. Query for lag:```sql
SELECT topic, max(lag) as peak FROM consumer_offsets WHERE consumer_group='service-processor' GROUP BY topic;
```

maria: owners/timelines recap: devon -> runbook appendix PR (Tue EOD), oliver -> alerts + canary job (72h), rachel -> add restart/validation commands to appendix (tomorrow noon), maria -> update RW-3680 & schedule retrospective check (today EOD).

ops-bot: Note: add weekly review reminder to on-call rotation calendar for this triage section (recurrence: every 6 weeks).

oliver: also proposing we instrument a small heap dump endpoint behind internal auth for deeper analysis if this recurs. I'll draft a design doc and attach to RW-3680. ETA 1 week.

maria: good idea. mark heap-dump as optional in runbook with explicit safety warnings.

devon: PR draft created: runbook/appendix/service-processor-triage. Will include commands, queries, escalation text, and checklist. Ping me for review.

rachel: adding a small note to the playbook release checklist: runbook changes must go through staging deploy and a pairing review with on-call before merging.

deploy-bot: Deployment triggered: runbook/appendix/service-processor -> staging (sha: b7c9d2)

maria: thanks everyone. we'll track close-out in RW-3680. If anyone needs to change ETA update the ticket and drop a note here. Closing loop next week during follow-ups meeting. :pray:
